target.title: fix(model-pricing): guard loopback host checks with isIP to prevent DNS SSRF bypass
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/gateway/model-pricing-cache.ts` contains a local copy of `isPrivateOrLoopbackHost` that checks `host.startsWith("127.")` / `host.startsWith("10.")` / `host.startsWith("192.168.")` without first verifying the value is an IPv4 literal.

A DNS hostname such as `127.evil.com` starts with "127." and would be incorrectly classified as loopback/private, allowing an attacker-controlled pricing endpoint URL to bypass the private-network restriction on model pricing cache refreshes — the same class of DNS SSRF bypass fixed for litellm in #110693.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an `isIP(host) === 4` guard so only real IPv4 addresses are matched by the private-range prefix checks. The IPv6 link-local (`fe80:`), unique-local (`fc`/`fd`), and localhost name branches are unchanged — DNS hostnames cannot collide with those prefixes.

Note: The canonical `isPrivateOrLoopbackHost` in `src/gateway/net.ts` already uses `normalizeIp` + `isPrivateOrLoopbackAddress` and is unaffected; the local copy in model-pricing-cache.ts is an outdated duplicate.

## Evidence

Base: 74880cb56f9 (origin/main). Head: bbea035e8b7.

```
$ node proof-model-pricing-ssrf.js
PASS: real loopback IP | host="127.0.0.1"
PASS: real private IP | host="10.0.0.1"
PASS: real private IP | host="192.168.1.1"
PASS: DNS hostname starting with 127 — BYPASS FIXED | host="127.evil.com"
PASS: DNS hostname starting with 10 — BYPASS FIXED | host="10.evil.com"
PASS: DNS hostname starting with 192.168 — BYPASS FIXED | host="192.168.evil.com"
PASS: normal hostname | host="example.com"
PASS: IPv6 loopback | host="::1"

All tests passed
```
